facts.statement: Liaoceratops lived approximately 126 million years ago during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It lived in the Early Cretaceous, 126 million years ago.

facts.statement: Liaoceratops was discovered in China by a team of American and Chinese scientists.
facts.quote: It was discovered in China by a team of American and Chinese scientists.

facts.statement: The species Liaoceratops yanzigouensis was named and described in 2002 by Xu Xing, Peter Makovicky, Wang Xiaolin, Mark Norell, and You Hailu.
facts.quote: The type species Liaoceratops yanzigouensis was in 2002 named and described by Xu Xing, Peter Makovicky, Wang Xiaolin, Mark Norell and You Hailu.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen IVPP V12738 was found in the Barremian-aged Yixian Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype IVPP V12738 has been found in the Yixian Formation dating from the Barremian.

facts.statement: In 2007, a skull of an even younger individual, specimen CAGS-IG-VD-002, was referred to the species.
facts.quote: In 2007 another skull, CAGS-IG-VD-002, of an even younger individual was referred.

facts.statement: A referred juvenile skull lacked its skull roof, which researchers explain as the result of a predator breaking the braincase to eat the contents.
facts.quote: This lacked the skull roof, which has been explained as the result of a predator opening the braincase to eat the contents.

facts.statement: The holotype skull measured 154 mm in length, weighed an estimated seven pounds, and possessed only jugal horns and a small frill, lacking the orbital horns and neck shield seen in later ceratopsians.
facts.quote: The holotype skull measures of 154 millimetres in length, weighing an estimated seven pounds and possessing only jugal horns and a small skull frill, lacking the orbital horns and true neck shield that characterized later ceratopsians.

facts.statement: Liaoceratops was small, weighing around 3 kg, with only incomplete traces of horns and a frill.
facts.quote: Liaoceratops es pequeño, pesando alrededor de 3 kilogramos y con solamente rastros incompletos de cuernos y un volante

facts.statement: Liaoceratops inhabited forest and wetland environments of the Jehol Biota during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Liaoceratops inhabited the forest and wetland environments of the Jehol Biota during the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Liaoceratops possessed an excellent sense of smell due to having large olfactory bulbs relative to its size.
facts.quote: Because Liaoceratops had large olfactory bulbs for its size, it possessed an excellent sense of smell.

facts.statement: Anatomical features suggest Liaoceratops had an almost horizontal head posture and was bipedal.
facts.quote: Its long semicircular canals and clearly distinguishable floccular lobes suggest that it had an almost horizontal head posture and that it was bipedal.

facts.statement: Short cochlear ducts suggest Liaoceratops individuals communicated through high-frequency vocalizations.
facts.quote: Its short cochlear ducts suggest that Liaoceratops individuals communicated with each other through high frequency vocalisations.

facts.statement: Liaoceratops belongs to the family Archaeoceratopsidae.
facts.quote: familia: Archaeoceratopsidae

facts.statement: Liaoceratops lived at the beginning of the Cretaceous period, approximately 126 million years ago, in the Barremian stage in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico , hace aproximadamente 126 millones de años,. en el Barremiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The small frill on the back of Liaoceratops's skull had clear marks for the insertion of chewing muscles.
facts.quote: El pequeño volante en la parte posterior de su cráneo estaba surcado por claras marcas para la inserción de los músculos masticatorios.

facts.statement: Liaoceratops had a small horn sheath on each side below its eyes.
facts.quote: Liaoceratops tiene un pequeño revestimiento de cuerno de cada lado debajo de sus ojos.

facts.statement: While initially thought to be offensive or defensive organs, many paleontologists now consider Liaoceratops's horns and frill to be display devices used for species recognition and attracting mates.
facts.quote: Primero se pensó que se trataba de órganos ofensivos o defensivos, estas estructuras son consideradas por muchos paleontólogos hoy como dispositivos de exhibición usados en el reconocimiento de la especie y atraer a compañeros.

facts.statement: The genus Liaoceratops was described by Xu and colleagues in 2002.
facts.quote: Xu et al. 2002

facts.statement: Liaoceratops belongs to the parent group Neoceratopsia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Neoceratopsia

facts.statement: Liaoceratops is classified within the dinosaur class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Liaoceratops lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are currently two recorded fossil occurrences of Liaoceratops in the scientific database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 2
